name: neural-painter
description: Neural Painter — f(x,y)→(r,g,b) implicit neural representation in PyTorch. Clean pipeline: Dataset/DataLoader, nn.Module forward(), loss.backward(), Trainer.train(), GPU handling. Live: https://neural-painter-production.up.railway.app

paragraphs: f(x, y) → (r, g, b) · A compact MLP that becomes an image — the same principle behind NeRF and SIREN, implemented in clean, debuggable PyTorch.

Instead of the conventional image → label classifier, Neural Painter learns a continuous function coordinate → color. Given any (x, y) in [-1, 1], the network predicts (r, g, b). After training, querying the network over a dense grid reconstructs the image — at any resolution, because the representation is continuous.
This is an implicit neural representation (INR). It reuses the same fundamentals as any production training pipeline while being visually interpretable and easy to debug.
features: Fully custom Dataset — CoordinateDataset generates (coord, color) pairs from any image; no external dataset download required (synthetic fallback included).
Fourier feature encoding — optional high-frequency encoding ([B,2] → [B,42]) for sharp reconstructions; toggle in config.yaml.
Two model variants — NeuralPainter (ReLU MLP) and SirenPainter (periodic activations) in model.py.
Manual + high-level training — train.py (explicit forward → loss → backward → step + model.to(device)) and traintrainer.py (transformers.Trainer.train() wrapper over the same pipeline).
Device-agnostic — auto / cuda / cpu via utils/helpers.getdevice(); all tensors and model moved explicitly.
